requirements.evidence: All contract routes are present with the right names, methods and middleware (routes/web.php:19-55, including throttle:6,1 on password.email and signed on verification.verify). Login (app/Livewire/Auth/Login.php:17-58) uses email:strict, a lowercased email+IP throttle key with 5 tries, auth.throttle/auth.failed on `email`, session regenerate and redirectIntended(default: route('home')). Register (app/Livewire/Auth/Register.php:36-57) uses the transliterate('register|'.$ip) key, Password::defaults() with confirmed, Registered, login, regenerate and redirectRoute('home'). Password::defaults() is set once (AppServiceProvider.php:25). NewPasswordController.php:42-48 rotates remember_token and fires PasswordReset. Forgot-password always flashes passwords.sent (PasswordResetLinkController.php:29-31). reset-password.blade.php has a single name="email". User implements MustVerifyEmail. EmailVerificationRequest returns 403 on a tampered id, and send() redirects verified users to home. Locale pins are in .env.example, config/app.php and phpunit.xml. Both ui.php files exist, and existing views now use route() and __().

conventions.evidence: #[Validate] + $this->validate() is used in both Livewire classes, $fillable is set via #[Fillable], inline $request->validate is used in controllers, and CHANGELOG/README are updated. Deviations: the user-creation write sits directly in the component (Register.php:44-48 `User::create([...])`) instead of an app/Actions class. The repeated Bulma field/label/error markup is copy-pasted across 4 views and the <head> across 3 layout files instead of being extracted into anonymous Blade components. Tests use `Event::fake` without importing the facade (PasswordResetTest.php, RegisterTest.php), unlike the other facades they import.

security.evidence: Login and register are rate-limited inside the method, and register hits the limiter before validation (Register.php:38-42). Email is strict. Forgot-password does not enumerate accounts. Logout invalidates the session and regenerates the token. Verification uses EmailVerificationRequest + signed + throttle. remember_token is rotated on reset. All output uses {{ }}, and no secrets sit in public properties. Minor gaps: the layouts and bulma-test load Bulma from cdn.jsdelivr.net without SRI as a fallback (guest.blade.php:14, app.blade.php:14). The forgot/reset routes are not behind the `guest` middleware (routes/web.php:32-44).

tests.evidence: Thorough Pest feature tests cover: login happy/invalid/strict-email/throttle/guest redirect (LoginTest.php), register happy/verification mail/unique/strict/password policy/confirmed/IP throttle (RegisterTest.php), logout guest/CSRF regeneration, forgot status for existing and missing e-mail plus 429, single email input, reset with remember_token rotation and PasswordReset, invalid token, verification tamper 403/invalid signature/resend/verified no-op/throttle, home redirects, and pt_BR/en localization. Missing: no Livewire tamper test (e.g. calling submit with client-set state that bypasses the UI), as the Livewire policy asks for. No test guards against hardcoded href/action in views. Register throttling is only tested by pre-seeding the limiter, not by real attempts.

simplicity.evidence: The controllers and components are direct and use framework features (Password broker, EmailVerificationRequest, RateLimiter). However, the same head block with the @vite/CDN fallback is duplicated in components/layouts/app.blade.php, components/layouts/guest.blade.php and bulma-test.blade.php. The field+label+@error markup is repeated about 10 times across the login/register/forgot/reset views. The guest/app layouts declare a `title` prop that no view ever passes, so the `ui.*.title` keys are unused.

readability.evidence: Small, well-named methods with PHPDoc (Login::throttleKey, Register::ensureIsNotRateLimited), consistent formatting, and clearly organized translation files. Minor: Register mixes #[Validate] attributes with a rules() method for password only (Register.php:20-29, 64-69). The `title` translation keys are dead (lang/*/ui.php).

scope.evidence: Translating existing views and replacing hardcoded links is in scope. Beyond that, welcome.blade.php is redesigned into a new landing page with login/register buttons. bulma-test.blade.php is rewritten from a fragment into a full HTML document with a CDN fallback and an unrelated link to home. The bulma-test route gains a name. The app layout adds a navbar.

issues.explanation: The user-creation write is done inline in the Livewire component instead of in an app/Actions class, which goes against the 'domain writes go through Actions' convention.
The document head with the @vite/CDN fallback is copy-pasted three times instead of shared.
The repeated Bulma field/label/input/@error markup is not extracted into an anonymous Blade component, as the UI conventions require.
The Livewire security policy requires a tamper test for each action, and none is provided; the register throttle is tested only by pre-seeding the limiter.
The welcome page is redesigned and the Bulma test page is rewritten into a full document with a CDN fallback and a home link, which goes beyond translating text and replacing hardcoded links.
The fallback loads third-party CSS from jsdelivr without Subresource Integrity.
The forgot/reset password routes are not inside the `guest` middleware group, so authenticated users can reach them.
The `ui.auth.*.title` keys and the layouts' `title` prop are never used, so every page title falls back to the app name.
Event::fake relies on the global facade alias without a `use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Event` import, unlike the other facades in the same files.

review.summary: The change implements the full session-auth flow (Livewire login/register, logout, forgot/reset password, e-mail verification) with pt_BR-first translations, a shared password policy, rate limiting and a comprehensive Pest suite, and it meets every requirement and contract detail. It loses points for convention deviations (no Action for user creation, no Blade components for repeated form markup, duplicated layout heads), unrequested redesigns of the welcome and Bulma test pages, and missing Livewire tamper tests. Approvable with minor follow-ups.
